name: beatZIG gen1
movedFrom: Until 2026-11-09 this CPU was cpus/release/gen1.mjs (named gen1) with gen1.json and the parts in cpus/release/gen1/. Only the names and the places changed: the weights, the features and the way it chooses did not.
what: Generation 1 of the learned CPU: one linear scorer over the candidates of a decision (flat), learned from a looking-ahead CPU's decisions, including the moves it left to the game's own CPU, with each decision weighted by how the match went (flat-all-value).

learnedFor.note: The rules the data was played under. When the game's rules change (the first-turn draw, a card, a rule version), the data and this CPU are of the old rules: learn it again.

learnedFrom.teacher: lookahead (k=2 determinized states, one move ahead)
learnedFrom.records: lookahead against lookahead (245 matches) and lookahead against simple in both seat orders (490 matches), every pair of the 7 start decks, seeds 101-105

validation.note: whole matches kept apart (20%); the share of decisions where the CPU's best move is the teacher's

method.loss: softmax over the candidates of a decision

evaluation.note: Strength = the share of matches won (a draw counts a half), both seat orders, every pair of start decks, game b8214a6; 95% range: Wilson.
evaluation.reference: lookahead itself wins 68.5% (65.5-71.3, 980 matches) against simple
evaluation.repeatability: played again from this file (seed 1 against simple, both orders, 98 matches): every match identical to the evaluation above (hash of the moves, result, turns, first player): 98/98; 60 won. Played again in a clean clone of the commit that made gen1 self-contained (nothing uncommitted): 98/98 identical again. With cpus/learned/policy.mjs deliberately broken in that clone, gen1 played 8 of those matches identically (it does not read cpus/learned/).

timePerDecision.note: choose() of the CPU: the candidates (the game's own planner, about 3.4 ms a call), the features and the scores. Milliseconds.

alone.source: measured on an idle machine (v3 report)

machineBusy.source: gen1 against itself, seed 1, 49 matches, while other runs were using the machine

playsOnly: what the seat can see: its own query (the observation and its legal actions). No look-ahead, no sim, no hidden information.

frozenCode.note: The CPU module imports only the copies in its own folder; cpus/learned/ and the others may change without changing how it plays. sha256 of each file with line endings read as LF; all = sha256 of the hashes in the order listed.
